items.q: In which part of the cell does glycolysis take place?
items.qAf: In watter deel van die sel vind glikolise plaas?
items.explain: Glycolysis splits glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm and needs no oxygen.
items.explainAf: Glikolise splits glukose na piruvaat in die sitoplasma en benodig geen suurstof nie.

items.q: What is produced by anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
items.qAf: Wat word deur anaërobiese respirasie in menslike spiersel geproduseer?
items.explain: Muscle cells without enough oxygen convert pyruvate into lactic acid.
items.explainAf: Spiersels sonder genoeg suurstof omskep piruvaat in melksuur.

items.q: Yeast in a sealed container without oxygen produces:
items.qAf: Gis in ’n toe houer sonder suurstof produseer:
items.explain: Yeast uses alcoholic fermentation, giving ethanol and CO₂.
items.explainAf: Gis gebruik alkoholiese gisting en gee etanol en CO₂.

items.q: Why does anaerobic respiration release less energy per glucose than aerobic respiration?
items.qAf: Hoekom stel anaërobiese respirasie minder energie per glukose vry as aërobiese respirasie?
options: Glucose is only partly broken down
items.explain: Without oxygen, the Krebs cycle and electron transport chain do not run, so most energy stays in the products.
items.explainAf: Sonder suurstof loop die Krebs-siklus en elektronoordragketting nie, dus bly meeste energie in die produkte.

items.q: Which stage of aerobic respiration produces the most ATP?
items.qAf: Watter stadium van aërobiese respirasie maak die meeste ATP?
items.explain: Most ATP is made by oxidative phosphorylation in the electron transport chain.
items.explainAf: Meeste ATP word deur oksidatiewe fosforilering in die elektronoordragketting gemaak.

items.qAf: Respirasie stel energie hoofsaaklik vry om:
items.explain: The energy is captured in ATP, which powers cell processes.
items.explainAf: Die energie word in ATP vasgevang, wat selprosesse aandryf.

items.q: The first stage of respiration, in which glucose is split into two pyruvate molecules in the cytoplasm.
items.qAf: Die eerste fase van respirasie, waarin glukose in die sitoplasma in twee piruvaatmolekules verdeel word.

items.q: The energy-carrying molecule made during respiration.
items.qAf: Die energiedraende molekule wat tydens respirasie gemaak word.

items.q: Respiration that takes place without oxygen.
The substance that builds up in muscles during anaerobic respiration.
items.qAf: Die stof wat tydens anaërobiese respirasie in spiere opbou.

items.text: The Krebs cycle takes place in the [[]] of the mitochondrion, and the electron transport chain takes place on the [[]].
items.textAf: Die Krebs-siklus vind in die [[]] van die mitochondrion plaas, en die elektronoordragketting vind op die [[]] plaas.

items.q: Aerobic respiration releases much more energy per glucose molecule than anaerobic respiration.
items.qAf: Aërobiese respirasie stel baie meer energie per glukosemolekule vry as anaërobiese respirasie.
items.explain: True. Aerobic respiration breaks glucose down completely to CO₂ and water.
items.explainAf: Waar. Aërobiese respirasie breek glukose heeltemal af tot CO₂ en water.

items.q: Yeast produces lactic acid during fermentation.
items.explain: False. Yeast produces ethanol (alcohol) and carbon dioxide.
items.explainAf: Onwaar. Gis produseer etanol (alkohol) en koolstofdioksied.

items.q: Put the stages of aerobic respiration in order.
items.qAf: Rangskik die fases van aërobiese respirasie in volgorde.

items.q: An athlete breathes deeply and quickly for a few minutes after a race. Explain why.
items.qAf: ’n Atleet asem vir ’n paar minute ná ’n wedloop diep en vinnig. Verduidelik waarom.
points: During the race the muscles respired anaerobically and lactic acid built up (an oxygen debt).
Extra oxygen is needed to break down the lactic acid (to CO₂ and water).
pointsAf: Tydens die wedloop het die spiere anaërobies gerespireer en melksuur het opgebou (’n suurstofskuld).
Ekstra suurstof is nodig om die melksuur af te breek (tot CO₂ en water).
